verdict.label: BUY — Oil Breaks $91; Nikkei Records; Tuesday Execution Armed
verdict.rationale_short: US markets were closed for Memorial Day, but the global session delivered one of the most significant macro developments in months: WTI crude fell ~5.2% to ~$90.65 as markets priced increasing Iran deal probability. Nikkei 225 hit a record all-time high above 65,000 for the first time; European STOXX 50 rose 2%; ES and NQ futures are positive into Tuesday. BUY maintained at medium conviction — the deal is unsigned, NVDA pre-market slipped below $215, and April PCE on Thursday remains the rate-path binary.

bear_case: Iran's willingness to signal progress publicly while simultaneously stating that signing is 'not imminent' is a negotiating posture that leaves maximum room for reversal. A formal Iranian denial before Tuesday's open would snap WTI from $91 back toward $99–103, eliminate the overnight yield relief this session is pricing in, and force SPX to open below 7,440 on gap-down with no liquid session to absorb the shock. NVDA's pre-market at $213.35 — below the prior brief's $215 execution threshold — reflects institutional position reduction, not accumulation; if Tuesday confirms a gap-down below $212, the two-session consolidation base is structurally impaired and the primary long thesis requires recalibration. April PCE on Thursday, with TradingKey warning that inflation is spreading across food, airfares, and AI chips, adds a second directional risk vector independent of Iran deal status. If SPX closes below 7,400 with the 30Y above 5.10% on any session through May 28, the BUY posture is abandoned and Step Aside is activated immediately.
